sources.entry: cloud-init - A multi-distribution package that handles early initialization of a cloud instance.

summary.one_liner: cloud-init is the multi-distribution industry-standard tool for early initialization of cloud instances from metadata, user data and vendor data.
summary.what_it_does: Cloud-init runs during boot on a disk image and identifies which cloud it is running on. It reads instance metadata from the cloud and uses it to initialize the system. Per the README, this can include setting up network and storage devices and configuring SSH access keys, among other system aspects. It also parses and processes optional user data and vendor data passed to the instance. The README says it is supported across major public cloud providers, private cloud provisioning systems, and bare-metal installs. The README is short and does not list specific supported distributions or clouds beyond saying most clouds and Linux/Unix OSes ship with it.
use_cases: initialize cloud virtual machines at first boot
configure networking and storage on cloud instances
inject SSH keys and user data into new instances
provision bare-metal or private cloud machines
standardize instance setup across multiple Linux distributions
notable: Processes cloud metadata, optional user data, and optional vendor data
Covers public cloud, private cloud, and bare-metal installs according to the README
Community support via a Matrix channel and GitHub Discussions
caveats: README does not include install or run instructions; it only points to the contributing guide for development
Support depends on the distribution or cloud; unsupported ones must be taken up with their maintainers
